title: prometheus-rules-gitops-sync-and-grafana-folders-per-tenant-automation
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Adds automated sync of Prometheus recording/alerting rules from a Git repo per-tenant, creates isolated Grafana folders+provisioning for each private install tenant, and wires Terraform/Helm hooks for safe upgrades and rollbacks. Backwards compatible with existing provisioning; customers must supply git repo and credentials in installer config.
description:
Motivation: Private installs increasingly host multiple logical tenants (teams/customers) inside a single VPC/on-prem deployment. We need automated, auditable propagation of Prometheus rules and Grafana dashboards per-tenant so alerts and runbooks remain consistent across upgrades and platform changes. This PR implements a GitOps-style rules sync operator plus a Grafana folder provisioning flow tied to the installer Terraform/Helm lifecycle.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight 'rules-sync' controller run as a sidecar in the observability namespace that watches a configured Git repo (with optional path per-tenant) and applies PrometheusRule CRDs via kubectl apply-style operations. The controller is implemented with idempotent apply semantics and leader-election for HA.
- Introduces Grafana provisioning templates that create a folder per-tenant and a folder-level permission model (read-only for general users, editors for tenant admins). Dashboards are synced from the same Git repo path and versioned by commit SHA.
- Extends the Terraform module to expose git repository, webhooks, and a helm_release hook pair to perform pre-upgrade validation and safe rollback on failure. The hook runs a dry-run of the rules sync and verifies no duplicate recording rules exist across tenants.
- Helm chart updates: adds templates for PrometheusRule, a ServiceAccount/Role for the rules-sync controller, and an init job that migrates legacy folder config to the new per-tenant model during upgrade.
- Adds a dashboard merge tool (small Go binary) used in CI to validate dashboards (UID collisions, panel schema) before applying. CI now includes a dashboard-validation job.

Commits summary: 6 commits (squashed on merge)
- feat(rules-sync): initial controller + leader-election + tests
- feat(grafana): folder provisioning templates + RBAC
- chore(terraform): expose git repo/webhook inputs and add pre/post hooks
- feat(ci): dashboard validation job and unit tests for merge tool
- fix(helm): init migration job to convert legacy folder labels
- docs: installer docs + upgrade notes

Files/areas changed (high level):
- terraform/modules/observability/main.tf (adds variables: rules_git_repo, rules_git_path, rules_git_branch, webhook_secret)
- helm/observability/templates/rules-sync-deployment.yaml (new controller)
- helm/observability/templates/grafana-provisioning.yaml (folder + datasource provisioning)
- helm/observability/templates/init-migrate-folders-job.yaml (upgrade migration)
- tools/dashboard-validate/main.go (new small tool used by CI)
- docs/private-installer/observability-gitops.md (usage and operator configuration)
- examples/tenant-configs/tenant-a.yaml (example repo layout and values.yaml snippet)

Small representative snippet (grafana provisioning):

apiVersion: 1
providers:
  - name: 'redwood-tenant-provisioning'
    orgId: 1
    folder: 'Tenant-${TENANT_ID}'
    type: file
    options:
      path: /var/lib/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/${TENANT_ID}

This provisioning file is templated at deploy time; the installer writes per-tenant folders and creates a Kubernetes secret with the commit SHA for traceability.

Operational considerations:
- Secrets: the git credentials are stored in a Kubernetes secret populated by Terraform; we added explicit KMS-encryption hooks in the Terraform module for cloud KMS/HSM users.
- Rollback safety: the helm pre-upgrade hook runs rules-sync in dry-run mode and the installer will abort an upgrade if rule collisions or invalid rule syntax are detected. The post-upgrade hook writes an upgrade marker commit SHA to the tenant namespace to allow automated rollbacks to lookup the previous dashboard state.
- Performance: rules-sync only re-applies changed manifests and has a configurable resync period; large repos should be scoped per-tenant path to avoid unnecessary churn.

CI and testing:
- New CI job 'obs/dashboard-validate' runs dashboard-validate against changed dashboard JSONs (checks UIDs, schema).
- 'obs/rules-integration' runs a k3s-based integration that exercises rules-sync against a fake Prometheus Operator and validates PrometheusRule CRDs are created.
- Initial CI run failed due to UID collision for an example dashboard; fixed by normalizing UID generation in dashboard-validate. Final CI status: pass.

Review convo (high level):
- Miguel Torres (reviewer): "This looks sound; main ask is to ensure the pre-upgrade dry-run is idempotent and won't mutate any CRDs. Also add a migration rollback test."
- Asha (author): "Added an explicit dry-run flag and created integration test 'obs/migration-rollback' that simulates a failed migration and validates the pre-upgrade marker prevents proceeding."
- Priya Shah (SRE): "We should avoid creating >1000 folders for clusters with many tenants — can we add an opt-out and on-demand provisioning?"
- Asha: "Added values.allowOnDemandFolderCreation (default: false). When true, the controller will create folders lazily on first dashboard access via an API hook. Documented trade-offs in the docs page."
- Dawson Lee: "Small nit: move the dashboard validation tool to tools/observability/dashboard-validate for consistency with other tools."
- Asha: "Moved the binary, updated CI job path."

Deployment notes / upgrade path for existing customers:
- Default behavior is backward compatible: if no rules_git_repo is provided, nothing changes.
- Customers opting in should supply a git repo and set values.rulesGit.path to their tenant subpaths. Terraform will create the secret; operator documentation explains repo layout conventions.
- For upgrades from earlier observability stacks that used a flat dashboard list, run the migration job first using the interactive installer flag --run-migration and review the generated migration plan in S3/artifacts.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Added Prometheus metrics for rules_sync_reconciles_total, rules_sync_errors_total, grafana_folder_creations_total, and dashboard_validation_failures_total.
- Dashboards: new 'Observability > Syncer' dashboard that surfaces per-tenant sync latency, last committed SHA, and applied rule counts.

Backwards compatibility and fallback:
- If rules-sync crashes or fails, the installer falls back to the previous release (helm rollback) using the recorded pre-upgrade marker. The terraform module includes a timeout and healthcheck to automate this in the managed upgrade flow.

Documentation: updated docs/private-installer/observability-gitops.md with examples, repo layout conventions, migration instructions, and troubleshooting (git auth, UID collisions).

Testing done: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests against k3s in CI, manual smoke tests in a staged private install cluster with two tenant namespaces.

Remaining follow-ups (tracked in linked Linear tasks):
- ENG-2248: Add webhook-based incremental sync to reduce full-repo scans.
- ENG-2307: Add RBAC refinement to map external identity providers to Grafana folder roles.

Merge outcome: PR was squashed and merged to main after approvals from Miguel, Priya, and Dawson. CI green on final run. Release notes added.

notes: This PR focuses on automation and safe upgrade paths for observability in private installs. It intentionally keeps defaults conservative to preserve backwards compatibility and adds opt-in features for tenants that want GitOps-driven alerts and dashboards.
example_values_snippet:
observability:
  rulesGit:
    repo: git@github.com:redwood/tenant-observability.git
    branch: main
    pathPrefix: tenants/${TENANT_ID}/rules
  grafana:
    enablePerTenantFolders: true
    allowOnDemandFolderCreation: false
  terraform_hooks:
    pre_upgrade_timeout: 300s
    enable_auto_rollback: true
